title: God's tefillin (Berakhot 6a)
hookLine: the Talmud imagines God's tefillin praising Israel, as ours praise God
tomorrow: if God prays, what would God pray for?

cards: On weekday mornings, some Jews wind black leather straps around an arm and set a small box on the head: tefillin. Inside are handwritten verses, among them, Hear, O Israel. Now the odd detail on Berakhot 6a.
The Talmud says God wears tefillin too. Which raises an obvious question: what's written inside God's?

teach.h: BY THE ARM OF HIS STRENGTH.
teach.b: First, the proof. Isaiah says: "The LORD hath sworn by His right hand, and by the arm of His strength." The Talmud reads the right hand as Torah, and the arm of strength as tefillin, the ones worn on the arm.
So God has tefillin. Then the real puzzle: what do they say?
Ours say: "Hear, O Israel: the LORD our God, the LORD is one."

teach.h: GOD'S: ONE NATION IN THE EARTH.
teach.b: God's, the Talmud answers, carry a verse from Chronicles: who is like Your people Israel, one nation in the earth. And God says: you made Me one in the world, and I will make you one in the world.
That's the puzzle solved. It's a mirror. Tefillin keep someone bound close, on the arm and between the eyes.
When people wear them, they carry God's oneness. When God wears them, in this picture, God carries the people.
That's today's line: God carries us. The page is describing a bond, the way two people who love each other each keep the other's photo close.
Here's one to tell a friend tonight: in the Talmud, God wears tefillin, and the verse inside is about the people who wear theirs. Two sets of straps, two arms, each holding the other in mind.

how: On weekday mornings many observant Jews put on tefillin for morning prayers, winding the arm strap and setting the head box; both hold handwritten passages, among them the Shema.

o: the tefillin the high priest wore inside the Temple
the Talmud's picture of God bound to the people in love

games.q: your little brother asks at dinner: we pray to God, but does God ever think about us back? what could you say from Berakhot 6a?
o: the Talmud pictures God wearing tefillin that praise the people, as ours praise God.
no; in the Talmud prayer only goes one way, from people up to God.
only on holidays, when the whole Torah scroll is read out loud.
games.why: Berakhot 6a's picture is a mirror: ours say God is one, God's say the people are one. each carries the other.

practice: Wrap the fingers of one hand gently around the other forearm, the way a strap is wound, and hold.
Think of one person who carries you in mind: your photo on their fridge, your name in their prayers, your number at the top of their phone. Let your hold stand for theirs, for the whole sit.

wordCard.voice: God's tefillin. The Talmud's picture of God bound to the people, as the people bind themselves to God.

orig.note: Hebrew: tefillin, the leather boxes and straps worn for weekday morning prayer.

carryVoice: Here it is: god carries us, and the straps are wound on both arms. Berakhot, day six.
